newsitem.title: BELGIUM: United Parcels extends services in Europe.
newsitem.headline: United Parcels extends services in Europe.

text.p: U.S. delivery group United Parcel Service on Wednesday launched a simplified "portfolio" of express services it said was part of its strategy to lead the $25 billion-a-year European package distribution market.
"Starting this week, our primary objective of the seamless portfolio of services throughout Europe is firmly in place," Ed Reitman, president of UPS Europe, told a news conference in Brussels.
"The same rates and pricing structure, the same documentation and paper work will apply whether a customer is shipping within a country or to another," he added.

UPS said the transformation and simplification of its range of services in Europe was part a $1.1 billion five-year investment plan for Europe into new technology, vehicles and infrastructure, which the company announced last year.

Reitman said UPS had already spent over a billion dollars in the past in Europe. Of the $1.1 billion announced last year "we have spent many millions to get to this point", he said, without specifying the exact figure.
The company estimated the European cross-border express market was currently growing in volume and revenue at rate of well over 10 percent a year.
Reitman said that in the past shippers had separate paperwork, procedures and service levels for national and intra-European deliveries and often two or more different bills.
UPS's service portfolio comprised three options - Express Plus, Express and Standard.
Express Plus, which gave delivery before 8 a.m., had been extended to major cities across Europe.
Express offered next day delivery by 10.30 a.m. to major metropolitan areas, with a new Saturday service, and Standard Service offered day-definite delivery across Europe, it said.

Reitman said UPS's five-year European investment plan included $300 million on aircraft, and $17 million would be spent this year on its main European air hub at Cologne. UPS currently had seven planes flying withing Europe, three flying across the Atlantic and 11 new charter flights.
In early 1997 UPS planned to open a European ground hub in Brussels at a cost of $16 million.
UPS said it had become the first customer of Global One -- a telecommunications venture between Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and U.S. company Sprint Corp.
This had allowed it to install a tracking system which made its package delivery information available worldwide within minutes, so improving customer service.
Privately-held UPS says it is the world's largest package distribution company, employing 335,000 people worldwide and providing services to more than 200 countries.
Revenues for 1995 amounted to $21 billion on a volume of 3.1 billion packages and documents.
